terms.definition: Where an object is located, measured relative to a chosen reference point.
terms.function: Names a location using a reference point plus a direction and a distance.
terms.whereItIs: A point — on a line, a number, a coordinate pair; not a length a rally has no extent.
terms.whyItMatters: Every other motion quantity (distance, displacement, speed, velocity) is a way of describing how position changes.

terms.definition: The fixed point that all measurements are compared against.
terms.function: Acts as the zero — move it and every position number changes, even though nothing moved.
terms.whereItIs: The 0 marker on the number line, the 'you are here' on a map, the origin of the grid.
terms.whyItMatters: A position number without a known reference point is meaningless.

terms.definition: A grid where each point is pinned by a pair of numbers — one per axis.
terms.whyItMatters: Lets one phrase (like (3, 2)) name a unique spot, the backbone of maps and graphs.
terms.whereItIs: The 2D grid overlay on the mat, with the object's (x, z) reading.

terms.definition: The zero point a coordinate system measures from — the reference point at the center.
terms.whyItMatters: It is the reference everything else answers 'where?' against: move it and all position numbers shift.
terms.whereItIs: The 0 marker and the (0,0) corner of the grid.
